reconcile.note: Clarke reads Kings' word for 'dead' as a participle meaning 'dying,' allowing Josiah to die in Jerusalem as Chronicles states.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats Chronicles' additions to Kings' account of Josiah's death at Megiddo as characteristic inventions, of which this location/timing divergence is an instance.

quotes.text: It is thus apparent how inventions of the most circumstantial kind have arisen out of this plan of writing history, as it is euphemistically called. One is hardly warranted, therefore, in taking the definiteness of statements vouched for by Chronicles alone as proof of their accuracy.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the unreliability of Chronicles' circumstantial additions to the Kings narrative.

sides.snippet: carried him in a chariot dead from Megiddo
sides.verseText: His servants carried him in a chariot dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb. The people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father's place.

sides.snippet: brought him to Jerusalem; and he died
sides.verseText: So his servants took him out of the chariot, and put him in the second chariot that he had, and brought him to Jerusalem; and he died, and was buried in the tombs of his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
